title: What is known about 1RB0RF_0LC1RE_---1LD_1LE0LB_0RF0LD_1RD1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_0LC1RE_---1LD_1LE0LB_0RF0LD_1RD1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the odd branch of the phase map for every odd e: C(2i+1) → C(3i+5), and the first, halving stage of the even branch for every even e ≥ 4: C(2i+4) reaches E> 110 (10)i 1100 (10)i+4. The rest of the even branch was tabulated by simulation for e ≤ 300: e ≡ 0 (mod 4) goes to (3e+6)/2, e ≡ 6 (mod 8) to (3e+12)/2, e ≡ 2 (mod 8) recursively, and e = 2k − 6 halts. Whether the blank orbit ever hits a halting value is the open question.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (C0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The odd branch of the map
claims.text: For every i: C(2i+1) → C(3i+5), i.e. e ↦ (3e+7)/2 for odd e, through P(a,b) = 0∞ 111 (0111)a 01 E> 0 (01)b: C(2i+1) → P(i,2), P(a+1,b) → P(a,b+3) in 6b+10 steps, P(0,b) → C(b+3).

claims.title: The even branch: the halving stage
claims.text: For every i, C(2i+4) reaches 0∞ E> 1 1 0 (10)i 1 1 0 0 (10)i+4: the 01-run is packed into 0111 words (even_pack), and then each 0111 becomes one 10 on each side of a marker 1100 (half0, half1, half, by induction halving). The next pass packs these 10s in pairs, so the continuation depends on the parity of i, which is the split e ≡ 0 / 2 (mod 4). Two later building blocks are proved as rules: E going left turns a 0111 word into three more 10s of the right-hand run (absorb_1011) and takes in a single 10 (absorb_10); chaining them into the whole even map is not done.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: Only C reading 0 halts; C is entered only from B reading 0 (0LC), so the machine halts exactly on 0 B> 0. Read off the table.

claims.title: The even branch, tabulated
claims.text: By simulation from C(e) for e = 1..300 (c/phasemap.c): odd e gives (3e+7)/2 every time (now proved); e ≡ 0 (mod 4), e ≥ 8, gives (3e+6)/2; e ≡ 6 (mod 8) gives (3e+12)/2; e ≡ 2 (mod 8) has no single formula (a cascade that halves the 01-run, e.g. 18 → 41, 74 → 101, 90 → 167); the machine halts from C(e) exactly for e = 2, 10, 26, 58, 122, 250 in that range, and also for 506 and 1018: e = 2k − 6.

claims.title: Why it is hard
claims.text: Like a Collatz map: the orbit grows by about 3/2 per phase, and it halts only if it lands on 2<sup>k</sup> − 6 (or on another halting value of the even cascade). A random-looking orbit hits such a sparse set with small probability, so it probably never halts, but nothing proves that.

claims.title: No closed tape language with small windows
claims.text: bbtools.ctl K = 3..6 leaves halting configurations; n-gram CPS fails; no invariant mod 2..12.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 41,952 cells have been visited and 23,260 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.04). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.552).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Lean proves the odd branch of the map; the even branch (and the halting values 2<sup>k</sup> − 6) are from simulation, and whether the blank orbit, now past C(70796), ever reaches a halting value is a Collatz-like question.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 41,952 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Blocks 0111 and a run of 01
html: Nearly always the tape is (0111)a (01)b, the head sweeping over it. At step 6·109 it is (0111)10042 (01)13065 E>0 (01)27606. Each sweep unpacks the last 0111 block, and the 01-run grows by three words; when the blocks are used up the run starts a new phase.

sections.heading: A Collatz-like map
html: Write C(e) = 0∞ 1 E> 0 (01)e 0∞. For odd e = 2i + 1 the head packs the 01-run into 111 (0111)i 01 E> 0 (01)2, unpacks one block per sweep adding three 01 words each time, and ends at C((3e+7)/2). Lean proves this for every odd e.

For even e the run packs differently and a halving cascade follows. Simulation gives (3e+6)/2 for e ≡ 0 (mod 4), (3e+12)/2 for e ≡ 6 (mod 8), a recursive outcome for e ≡ 2 (mod 8), and a halt for e = 2k − 6 (2, 10, 26, 58, 122, 250, 506, 1018).

Even e starts the same way every time, and Lean proves that start for all even e ≥ 4: the run of 01s is packed into 0111 words, and then a sweep halves them: each 0111 turns into one 10 on each side of a marker 1100, so C(2i+4) becomes E> 110 (10)i 1100 (10)i+4. The next pass packs the 10s two at a time, so what happens next depends on whether i is even or odd; that is where the cases e ≡ 0 and e ≡ 2 (mod 4) part, and the e ≡ 2 case halves again, which gives the cascade.

sections.heading: Only if the orbit lands on a halting value
html: The machine stops only on 0 B> 0. From blank tape the orbit is 4, 17, 29, 47, 74, 101, 155, ..., 47195, 70796 (step 9.4·109), growing by about 3/2 each phase. It halts if it ever lands on a halting value of the even branch, such as 2k − 6. So far it has not.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.04). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.552).
After 109 steps the tape spans 41,952 cells (38 left of the start, 36,840 right), with a density of 1s of 0.554.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A Collatz-like map on C(e) = 0^inf 1 E> 0 (01)^e: odd e goes to (3e+7)/2 (proved in Lean for every odd e); even e takes a halving cascade, and e = 2^k - 6 halts. The blank run passes C(4), C(17), ..., C(70796) by step 9.4·10^9.
